items: Global warming: the long-term rise in the Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities; the IPCC (2023) reports about 1.1 C of warming compared with 1850-1900.

Heatwaves: cities such as Jacobabad and Sibi are among the hottest places on Earth; above 50 C the body cannot keep its normal temperature and heatstroke can be fatal. Livestock suffer heat stress, warmer winters let pests and mosquitoes survive longer, droughts worsen and wildfires become more likely.

Floods: warmer air holds more moisture, giving erratic, intense rain and 'turbo-charged' monsoons that damage forests, homes and crops, erode and deplete soil, contaminate water and spread water-borne diseases.

Glacial melting: Pakistan has more glaciers than anywhere outside the polar regions; glaciers such as Baltoro and Batura are melting fast, causing glacial lake outburst floods, and if they vanish the Indus could run dry.
Sea-level rise and coastal erosion: melting ice and warming water raise the sea; in Thatta and Badin seawater is turning farmland into salty marshes.
Food insecurity: heat at flowering cuts wheat and rice yields, and heat-dried soils turn into desert (desertification).
Ecosystem disruption: fast changes in temperature and rainfall force species to move or migrate and can drive them to extinction.

blocks.title: Tidbits: floods, GLOFs and cloudbursts
blocks.text: In June 2025, floods in Pakistan, caused by heavy pre-monsoon rain, glacial lake outburst floods and cloudbursts, caused over 1,000 deaths, displaced over 3 million people and destroyed over 200,000 homes. A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) is a sudden release of water when a glacial lake's natural dam, for example of ice, breaks; its water can travel over 100 km. A cloudburst is sudden, extremely heavy rain over a small area in a short time.
